title: Relative generation and polynomial multiplication from fibre regularity
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq0$, $m\geq1$, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X=\mathbf P^n_T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with $Z\to T$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Put $p:X\to T$, $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, $K_b=p_*\mathcal I(b)$ and $V_e=\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_e$, using twists [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and ordinary pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Suppose $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and its canonical pullback to each geometric fibre is the ideal $\mathcal I_{\bar t}$ of $Z_{\bar t}\subset\mathbf P^n_k$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Assume these fibre ideals are coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and $m$-regular, meaning $H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal I_{\bar t}(m-j))=0$ for $1\leq j\leq n$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. Suppose, for every integer $b\geq m$, that $K_b$ is finite locally free (locally a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O_T$) and the canonical map $\bar t^*K_b\to H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal I_{\bar t}(b))$ is an isomorphism. Then the canonical evaluation map
$$p^*K_m\otimes\mathcal O_X(-m)\longrightarrow\mathcal I$$
is surjective, and for every integer $d\geq m$ the canonical multiplication map
$$V_{d-m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}K_m\longrightarrow K_d$$
is surjective. The multiplication map here is the one induced by multiplying sections of $\mathcal O_X(d-m)$ with sections of $\mathcal I(m)$, using the monomial identification $p_*\mathcal O_X(d-m)=V_{d-m}$.

source.place: Tags 08A6 (lemma-m-regular-up), 08A7 (lemma-m-regular-multiply), 08A8 (lemma-m-regular-globally-generated), 00DV (lemma-NAK); fibrewise evaluation and iterated multiplication descended by local Nakayama

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$ and write $q:X_{\bar t}\to X$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal I_{\bar t}$. The hypotheses identify $q^*\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal F$ and $\bar t^*K_m$ with $H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(m))$. The twist transition functions pull back to the same functions $(x_i/x_j)^b$; thus $q^*\mathcal O_X(b)=\mathcal O_{X_{\bar t}}(b)$. Pullback commutes with tensor products. Consequently the pullback of the evaluation map, after tensoring by $\mathcal O(m)$, is the evaluation $H^0(\mathcal F(m))\otimes_k\mathcal O\to\mathcal F(m)$. This identifies the actual map: on a standard chart its value on a pulled-back section $s$ and the local basis of $\mathcal O(-m)$ is the restriction of $s$ times that basis. The canonical section base-change map in the hypothesis sends $s$ to exactly this restriction. The regularity node, applied with $a=b=m$, makes this evaluation surjective. Tensoring by the inverse local basis untwists it, so $q^*$ of the original evaluation is surjective.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the cokernel of the original evaluation, and fix $x\in X$. Its stalk $C_x$ is a quotient of the finite $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $\mathcal I_x$, hence finite. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$ and the corresponding point $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. Its composite with $p$ is a geometric point of $T$, so $a$ factors through a geometric fibre where step 1 gives a surjective evaluation. Pullback preserves this surjectivity: its stalk maps are scalar extensions, and tensor is right exact. By the natural pullback-stalk formula and right exactness, $C_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\Omega=0$. The local-ring map to $\Omega$ factors through $\kappa(x)$, so this tensor product is $(C_x/\mathfrak m_x C_x)\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\Omega$. The nonzero-vector-space tensor lemma forces $C_x/\mathfrak m_x C_x=0$. Apply the submodule form of local Nakayama to $0\subset C_x$ to conclude $C_x=0$. Stalk exactness and the Zariski stalkwise surjectivity criterion now prove that the evaluation is surjective on $X$.

Still on $\mathbf P^n_k$, put $W_r=H^0(\mathcal F(m+r))$ for $r\geq0$. The regularity node makes each $W_r\otimes_k H^0(\mathcal O(1))\to W_{r+1}$ surjective. By the projective twist cohomology formula, $H^0(\mathcal O(1))$ has basis $x_0,\ldots,x_n$. Inductively every element of $W_r$ is a finite sum $\sum_{|\alpha|=r}x^\alpha s_\alpha$ with $s_\alpha\in W_0$: for $r=0$ use $1\cdot s$; for the successor first write a section as $\sum_i x_i t_i$, expand each $t_i$ by induction, and collect the monomials $x_i x^\alpha$. Therefore $k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_r\otimes_k W_0\to W_r$ is surjective. This includes $n=0$, with the single coordinate $x_0$; the induction uses only nonnegative polynomial degrees.

Fix $d\geq m$ and put $r=d-m$. Under $\bar t^*K_b=H^0(\mathcal F(b))$ for $b=m,d$, the pullback of $\mu_d:V_r\otimes K_m\to K_d$ is the polynomial multiplication of step 3. Indeed $V_r$ is free on the finitely many degree-$r$ monomials; tensoring its coefficients gives $\bar t^*V_r=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_r$. Pullback of the source tensor is the tensor of the pullbacks. For a local section $s$ of $K_m$ and a monomial $x^\alpha$, the section base-change map sends $\mu_d(x^\alpha\otimes s)=x^\alpha s$ to $x^\alpha\bar s$, since restriction preserves scalar multiplication and the twist pairing has the chart formula of step 1. Thus the two maps agree on generators, hence on all tensors. In particular $\bar t^*\mu_d$ is surjective for every geometric point.

Let $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Coker}(\mu_d)$ on $T$ and fix $t\in T$. Its stalk $D_t$ is a quotient of $(K_d)_t$, which is finite free by hypothesis, so $D_t$ is finite. Choose $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(t)}$. Step 4, the natural pullback-stalk formula and right exactness give $D_t\otimes_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}\Omega=0$, equivalently $(D_t/\mathfrak m_tD_t)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\Omega=0$. The nonzero-vector-space tensor lemma implies $D_t/\mathfrak m_tD_t=0$, and local Nakayama gives $D_t=0$. Stalk exactness and the Zariski stalkwise criterion prove $\mu_d$ surjective. This holds separately for every $d\geq m$. When $d=m$, its fibre calculation is simply multiplication by $1$; when $T$ is empty, both claims are vacuous because all the sheaves are zero.
